name: needle
pitch_zh: 畫面全暗，中央只有一道細細的刻度，別無他物。一根髮絲般的指針從左邊盪進來，衝過刻度，顫著退回，又稍稍過頭，最後正正停在記號上。它停住的那一瞬，畫面像反光鏡抬起般眨了一下，Aoraki 的照片就整張在那裡，填滿視窗，沒有任何淡入。
pitch_en: The window is dark, with one thin notch at its centre and nothing else. A hair-thin needle swings in from the left, overshoots the notch, quivers back, creeps a little too far again and settles exactly on the mark. The instant it rests there is a blink, like a mirror lifting, and the Aoraki photograph is there whole, filling the window, with no fade.
build: A dark stage with an SVG needle driven by a damped spring in requestAnimationFrame (about 2.2 s of swing, overshoot and settle), then an 80 ms black blink and the stage removed in one frame; the cover beneath is never touched, so the hand-over is exact. About 3.5 s.
source: A camera mechanism, read from Wikipedia and two owners' accounts (Jim Grey's blog, Photoethnography); not handled here.
quality: A single thin needle that swings, overshoots, damps and comes to rest on a mark, and that rest is the cue on which the photograph arrives whole.

name: charcoal
pitch_zh: 溫暖的紙。炭筆在上面出現，是大片深色的擦痕而不是線條：山稜、山頂背光的那一面、車窗框的暗部，用照片本身的深色調在兩秒內鋪上。接著一陣風把炭粉帶走，向右吹散，粉塵散開的地方，Aoraki 的照片原來一直在底下，清晰而完整。
pitch_en: Warm paper. Charcoal appears on it in broad dark rubbings, not lines: the ridge, the summit's shadowed side, the dark of the car window frame, laid down in the photograph's own tones over two seconds. Then one gust takes the dust, streaming it off to the right, and where it clears the Aoraki photograph was underneath all along, sharp and full.
build: A canvas over the cover: the lead image sampled small, its dark pixels drawn as grainy charcoal strokes over about 2 s, then each dark pixel released as a particle in a wind field (about 1.2 s) while the canvas's own alpha is wiped in the wind's direction; the cover beneath is untouched. About 4 s.
source: Art of the Title interview page (read in full; quotes from it). Description only, no video watched.
quality: The charcoal that is blown off: the ridge and horizon rubbed onto paper in the photograph's own dark tones (tone, not thin line), and one gust carries the dust off the page so that what remains under it is the photograph. For the router: an alternative execution of the ridgeline concept he kept, with a different material and a different reveal; not darkroom, since nothing emerges slowly, the dust leaves in one gust.

name: stamp
pitch_zh: 空白的暖紙，停一口氣。一片整個視窗大的影子從上方壓暗下來，Aoraki 的照片一拍蓋在紙上，落下時稍大，隨即壓平。半秒鐘裡墨色不均，受壓處飽滿、一邊較淡，然後勻開，印痕平貼，就是首頁的封面。
pitch_en: Blank warm paper for a breath. A shadow the size of the whole window darkens from above, and the Aoraki photograph is pressed down onto the paper in one beat, landing slightly larger and settling flat. For half a second the ink is uneven, full under the pressure and thinner along one edge, then it evens out and the print lies flat as the page's cover.
build: A full-window copy of the photograph on the paper stage, scaled 1.05 under a soft block shadow, pressed to 1.0 in about 160 ms (ease-in); at contact an SVG mask of ink density (a gradient thinning toward one edge, feTurbulence grain) evens to full over 500 ms, then the stage fades over the identical cover. About 3 s with the paper beat before.
source: Art of the Title interview page (read; quotes from it) and a 2003 Stopdesign note on the method. Descriptions only.
quality: The stamp: the photograph lands on the paper the way a carved stamp does, pressed down in one beat from a small height, the ink full where the pressure is and lighter at one edge, a thin shadow of the block for an instant before it meets the paper, then the block is gone and the print lies flat as the cover. A photographer's object too (his seal goes on the back of a print). Nearest neighbour is projector (gravity drop into a gate with a bounce); here it is pressure onto paper, no gate, no bounce, no dark stage.

name: tube
pitch_zh: 全黑。一道刺眼的橫帶滾下視窗又滾回去，像電視機失去垂直同步，然後啪地歸黑。接著 Aoraki 的照片在三秒裡從黑暗中慢慢浮亮，起初稍亮稍豔，帶著細細的掃描線，隨著線條消失，回到它真正的色彩。
pitch_en: Black. A blinding horizontal band rolls down the window and back up, like a television losing its vertical hold, and snaps to black. Then the Aoraki photograph blooms up out of the dark over three slow seconds, a little too bright and too saturated at first, with faint scanlines, and settles to its true colour as the lines vanish.
build: A dark stage holding a copy of the photograph: a Web Animations keyframe with transform scaleY and filter brightness for the 0.4 s roll, 0.1 s of black, then opacity with a brightness and saturate overshoot easing back to none over 3 s under a repeating-linear-gradient scanline layer that fades with the stage. About 4 s; the cover beneath is unfiltered.
source: CodePen, the full SCSS read in the browser, not run
quality: Two beats at two speeds, a violent short one and a slow long one, so the picture's arrival has a rhythm instead of an ease.

name: rubbing
pitch_zh: 溫暖的紙。一道寬寬的筆觸從左到右掃過，筆觸裡就是照片：Aoraki 的山稜，已經清晰。下一道折回來，加上下方的冰河，再來是天空，再來是車窗深色的邊，每一道都像拓印的墨包一樣一點一點往前拍，到第六道補滿最後的空隙，整張照片都在了。
pitch_en: Warm paper. One broad stroke crosses it from left to right, and inside the stroke is the photograph: the ridge of Aoraki, already sharp. The next pass turns back and adds the glacier below, then the sky, then the car window's dark edge, each stroke dabbing forward in small steps like an ink pad, until the sixth pass fills the last gap and the whole photograph is there.
build: An SVG mask over a full-window copy of the photograph on the paper stage: a polyline with a stroke about a fifth of the window's height, revealed by stroke-dashoffset in six to seven passes with steps() timing, about 3 s; when the mask is full the stage fades and the cover beneath is identical.
source: Dudley Storey's tutorial (code read); Penn State and museum pages on Chinese stone rubbings; read, not watched
quality: The picture delivered by strokes of a visible hand, each stroke a window, not a drawing.

name: tinting
pitch_zh: Aoraki 的照片已經在那裡，完整而清晰，卻是溫暖的深褐色，像一張老蛋白印相。一抹藍刷進天空，稍稍越過邊緣，然後定住；雪維持白色；赭黃進了草坡，一點淡綠進了車窗玻璃，每一筆都是獨立的決定，相隔一拍。最後一筆完成，它就是彩色照片。
pitch_en: The Aoraki photograph is already there, whole and sharp, but in warm sepia like an old albumen print. A wash of blue is brushed into the sky, slightly past its edge, and settles; the snow stays white; ochre goes into the tussock, a faint green into the car glass, each a separate decision a beat apart. The last wash finishes it and it is the colour photograph.
build: A sepia copy of the photograph (CSS filter) over the cover, cut away region by region through an SVG mask of four or five soft-edged paths drawn for this photograph, each a little larger than the true edge, growing one after another over about 4 s; when the mask is full the copy goes and the cover is unchanged.
source: Wikipedia; Musée des Arts Décoratifs collection page (nearly 700 hand-coloured Japanese travel photographs); read, not watched
quality: Colour arriving area by area as washes, each with a brush's soft overshoot, over a photograph that was already whole.

name: woodblock
pitch_zh: 空白的紙。第一版輕輕一壓落下：最淡的平面色塊，天空和雪。第二版帶來山稜的中間調，第三版是陰影，第四版是車窗框的深色，每一版都正正對位落下，帶一點頓感。最後一版就是照片本身，平面的疊層一下子變成連續色調的 Aoraki。
pitch_en: Blank paper. The first impression lands with a soft press: the palest flat shapes, sky and snow. The second brings the mid-tones of the ridges, the third the shadows, the fourth the dark of the car window frame, each landing exactly in register with a small thump. The last impression is the photograph itself, and the flat stack snaps into Aoraki in continuous tone.
build: The photograph posterised into five luminance levels on a canvas pass (or stacked copies with feComponentTransfer discrete tables), each level faded in over 150 ms with a one-pixel settle, about 600 ms apart, the true photograph last; about 4 s, ending on the cover beneath with the canvas removed.
source: Asian Art Museum (San Francisco) education page; Viewing Japanese Prints FAQ; the British Museum Hiroshige blog via its search summary (page refused a fetch); read, not watched
quality: Assembly by impressions, lightest first, each landing as one flat press, the photograph as the final impression.

name: shoji
pitch_zh: 一面背光的紙屏填滿視窗，隱約看得見格子，上面有一道影子：Aoraki 的山稜、山頂和車窗柱柔柔的灰色剪影，在照片出現之前就先讀到了。靜止一拍。然後紙門一拉滑開，細細的木框條劃過視窗，後面的照片從第一毫米起就清晰完整。
pitch_en: A backlit paper screen fills the window, its faint lattice showing, and on it is a shadow: the soft grey silhouette of Aoraki's ridge and summit and the car window pillar, read before any photograph exists. A beat of stillness. Then the panel slides aside in one pull, its thin wooden stile travelling across the window, and the photograph behind is sharp and full from the first millimetre.
build: The stage is the paper panel with a repeating-gradient lattice and a blurred, greyscale, multiplied copy of the photograph as the shadow; after a 1.2 s hold the panel translates off the window in 0.7 s (ease-in-out) with a dark stile at its leading edge, and done() fires as it clears; the cover beneath is untouched. About 3 s.
source: Lafcadio Hearn's Kyoto journal (the peach-tree shadow on the shoji) via Writers in Kyoto, plus the Wikipedia Shoji entry (washi over a kumiko lattice, panels sliding in grooves)
quality: The photograph known first as its own shadow on the page, read before it is seen, then the page itself slid aside in one pull.

name: hanging
pitch_zh: 紙頁視窗的頂端掛著一卷緊緊的橫軸，照片本身的顏色裹在一根細細的深色軸上。它落下來：軸桿一墜，Aoraki 在半秒內從天空到草坡在它後面展開，卷軸的弧度帶著畫面繞過軸桿。到底後過頭一掌寬，盪回一次，靜靜垂住；軸桿消失，照片就是封面。
pitch_en: At the top of the paper window hangs one tight horizontal roll, the photograph's own colours wrapped round a thin dark rod. It drops: the rod falls and Aoraki unrolls behind it from sky to tussock in half a second, the curve of the roll carrying the picture round the rod. It reaches the bottom, overshoots a hand's width, swings back once and hangs still; the rod goes and the photograph is the cover.
build: The cover revealed by clip-path inset animated from the top over about 0.55 s with a gravity ease, a roll element (a squashed, shaded strip of the photograph) riding the edge, and the rod continuing a few percent past the bottom and springing back once (Web Animations, about 0.4 s); the stage then fades over the cover. About 3 s with the hold before the drop.
source: Wikipedia's Hanging scroll entry (the weighted bottom rod, digan, that makes it hang and lets it roll; scrolls shown briefly then rolled and tied) and the National Palace Museum's animated scroll project, theme.npm.edu.tw/exh112/npm_anime/RedCliff/en
quality: The photograph arriving as its own rolled sheet falling open, the weight of the rod making the bounce, in the gesture of a hanging scroll.

name: grad
pitch_zh: Aoraki 的照片已經是封面，卻是相機沒上濾鏡時看到的樣子：天空和雪過曝成紙白，下方的地景正常。一片透明的濾片從上緣滑下來，上半部深色、邊緣是柔和的漸層，它滑過的天空一路回來，藍、雲、山頂的雪有了層次。濾片的邊緣停在山稜上，像卡進濾鏡座一樣穩穩一頓，然後它的輪廓消失。
pitch_en: The Aoraki photograph is already the cover, but as the camera saw it without a filter: the sky and the snow blown to paper white, the land below correct. From the top edge a clear sheet slides down, dark in its upper half with a soft gradient edge, and as it descends the sky it covers comes back, blue, cloud, the summit's snow given its tone. It stops when its edge lies on the ridge, with a small firm settle like a filter seating in its slots, and its outline is gone.
build: The cover beneath; over it a brightened copy of the photograph masked to the sky with a soft lower edge; an outlined sheet descends over about 1.4 s (ease-out) and drives the mask's clip-path inset from the top, stopping at the ridge's fraction of the window computed from fit(), with a 6 px overshoot and settle; then the copy and the outline fade. About 3.5 s.
source: Wikipedia's Graduated neutral-density filter entry (a rectangular filter slid in a holder, the transition set on the horizon, soft edge for mountains) and the Lee 100 landscape kit page at glazerscamera.com
quality: The sky arriving by a dark sheet sliding down to the horizon and seating there, the photographer's grad filter at full size.

name: slab
pitch_zh: 視窗是一整張完好的暖紙。一道裂痕在靠近頂端處快速劃過，鋸齒狀，接著兩道沿兩側裂下。裂痕以下整片鬆脫往下滑，墜落中斷成四塊，塊與塊之間裂開細縫，一塊接一塊離開底邊，Aoraki 的照片就是它滑落後露出的地面，從第一道裂痕起就是清晰的；裂痕上方的一條紙停一拍，然後也走了。
pitch_en: The window is unbroken warm paper. A crack runs across it near the top in one quick jagged line, then two run down the sides. The whole sheet below the crack lets go and slides downward, breaking into four blocks as it falls, thin gaps opening between them, each leaving the bottom edge in turn, and the Aoraki photograph is the ground beneath, sharp from the first crack; the strip above the crown holds a beat and goes.
build: The paper stage split into a top strip and four polygon blocks by clip-path on copies; the crack drawn as an SVG stroke with dashoffset over 150 ms, then the blocks translateY out with a gravity ease and a few degrees of rotation, staggered 60 ms, about 0.9 s, the top strip fading after 0.5 s; the cover beneath is untouched. About 3 s with the still paper first.
source: Wikipedia's Slab avalanche entry (crown fracture at the top of the start zone, flank fractures at the sides, the slab breaking into blocks and accelerating under its own weight, the bed surface left bare)
quality: The page let go all at once along a fracture line and sliding out of the frame under its own weight, the photograph the ground it slid off.

name: inkjet
pitch_zh: 視窗頂端一道深色的出紙口，下面是空白的紙。紙一格一格往下送，一次一條，Aoraki 的照片跟著出來：先是天空，再是山稜，再是草坡，每一條由兩次快速的來回鋪上，一道細細的噴頭影子從左掃到右，條帶下緣先是濕亮的，一瞬間乾成霧面。最後一條離開出紙口，出紙口消失，印好的作品就是封面。
pitch_en: A dark slot across the top of the window, the printer's mouth, and blank paper below it. The paper feeds down in steps, a band at a time, and the Aoraki photograph comes with it: sky first, then the ridge, then the tussock, each band laid in two quick passes as a thin carriage shadow crosses left to right, its lower edge glossy for an instant before drying matte. The last band clears the slot, the slot goes, and the finished print is the cover.
build: The cover revealed by clip-path inset from the top in about 24 bands with steps() timing (one every 120 ms, about 3 s), a highlight strip on the newest band fading in 300 ms and a translucent carriage shadow sweeping it; a dark slot element at the top of the stage fades with the stage. Ends on the unclipped cover.
source: Wikipedia's Inkjet printing entry (the carriage crossing the paper while the paper advances a band at a time, multiple passes, the print emerging from the front) and Epson's SureColor P-series announcement at australianphotography.com
quality: The photograph arriving as a print being made, fed out band by band with the carriage's crossing rhythm, so the picture is seen being finished rather than revealed.

name: timer
pitch_zh: 畫面是暖色的紙，只有正中偏下一個小小的光點，像相機前面那顆自拍計時燈。它先慢慢地閃，一秒一下，閃四下，你會不自覺地跟著數；接著突然變快，閃一秒多，就像每一台相機按下快門前那樣。燈定住，紙一下子不見，Aoraki 從車窗裡整面出現，好像是你走出了畫面，相機替你按下的。
pitch_en: The window is warm paper, empty but for one small dot low in the middle, the colour of a camera's timer lamp. It blinks slowly, once a second, four times, long enough that you count without meaning to; then it quickens for a second, the way every camera does before it fires. The lamp holds, and in one cut the paper is gone and Aoraki fills the window through the car glass, as if you had stepped out of the frame and the camera had taken it.
build: A paper stage from o.stage() with a 10px disc in the clay token, blinked by one stepped Web Animations keyframe (four beats at 1 s, then six at 180 ms, about 5.5 s in all); on the last beat the opening removes the stage itself in one frame and calls o.done(null, 0), so the photograph beneath is simply there, the cover untouched.
source: Canon camera manual (also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self_timer); read, and known from use of any camera since the 1970s
quality: A countdown told only by tempo: one small light blinking slow and then fast, and then the picture, with no number anywhere.

name: fan
pitch_zh: 暖色的紙，底邊正中一個點，照片像摺扇被手腕一甩，從那個點扇形地彈開：弧線不到一秒從左掃到右，Aoraki 的天空、雪、車窗的黑框一根根扇骨地到來，摺痕的地方有淡淡的光帶。最後一根扇骨停在邊上，輕輕一頓，多走幾度又彈回來，摺痕的光隨之攤平。留下的就是整面的照片，就是封面本身。
pitch_en: Warm paper, and from a point at the bottom centre a thin sector of the photograph flicks open, the way a fan snaps open in one wrist: the arc sweeps from left to right in well under a second, Aoraki's sky, the snow and the dark window frame arriving rib by rib, with faint bands of light where the pleats would be. The last rib stops against the edge with a tiny knock, an overshoot of a few degrees and back, and the pleats flatten away. What is left is the photograph, full window, exactly the cover.
build: A paper stage holding a full-window copy of the lead image (o.src(lead), object-fit cover) under a CSS conic-gradient mask centred at 50% 100%, its angle set per frame from -90 to +90 degrees on a snap ease with one 3-degree overshoot in about 0.7 s, plus a repeating-conic-gradient of faint white bands that fades out over the last 0.3 s; about 1.5 s in all, then o.done fades the stage over the identical cover.
source: Princeton University Art Museum object page (Lan Ying, Landscape in the Style of Huang Gongwang, folding fan mounted as album leaf, ink and colour on gold-flecked paper, 16 x 50.3 cm), the 中文 Wikipedia entry on the fan's parts, and the National Palace Museum folding-fan exhibition; read. The gesture of opening a fan is from life.
quality: The picture unfolds from a pivot in one flick and stops with a knock: the snap of a fan.

name: histogram
pitch_zh: 紙上靠下、橫向寬寬的一道灰色圖表從左邊開始升起：二百五十六根細細的直條，一根接一根，每一根都是 Aoraki 那張照片裡那個色階真實的像素數，直接從照片讀出來。先是陰影，低低一片；然後岩石和灰天的中間調爬成一座山丘；接近右邊，雪拉出一根尖尖的高峰。大約兩秒，看起來就像一道山脈，因為它本來就是。最後一根落下的瞬間，圖表一刀切掉，被它量過的那張照片整面出現。
pitch_en: On the paper, low and wide, a grey graph starts to rise from the left: 256 thin bars, one after another, each the true count of that tone in the Aoraki photograph, read from the picture itself. Shadows first, a low mass; then the mid-tones of rock and grey sky climb into a hill; then, near the right, the snow sends up a sharp spike. It takes about two seconds and it looks like a mountain range, because it is one. As the last bar lands, the graph is gone in one cut and the photograph it measured is there, full window.
build: After o.ready, draw the lead image to a 512px offscreen canvas and count a 256-bin luminance histogram; on a paper stage an SVG draws the bars in the ink token with no axis or number, bar i growing in at i times 7 ms on o.easeOut over 300 ms (about 2.2 s in all); at the last bar the stage is removed in one frame and o.done(null, 0) hands over the cover, which was never touched.
source: Wikipedia entry on the image histogram (field use at https://www.cambridgeincolour.com/tutorials/histograms1.htm, which refused a plain fetch today); read, and known from every camera's back
quality: The picture's own measurement drawn on paper first, true to the pixel, becoming the picture.

name: fence
pitch_zh: 照片從第一格就整面在那裡，只是隔著一排紙柵：寬寬的紙板中間只留細縫，縫裡只看得到 Aoraki 的一條條碎片，看不出是什麼。整排柵欄開始橫向移動，像車子開動時路邊的籬笆：先慢，縫裡的碎片一直換；然後越來越快，快到紙板糊成一層半透明的灰，整座山就這樣穩穩地從柵欄後面透出來，就像高速下看籬笆那樣。柵欄滑出畫面邊緣，照片留下，一點沒變。
pitch_en: The photograph is there from the first frame, full window, but behind a wall of paper palings: wide paper boards with narrow slits between, and through the slits only slivers of Aoraki, unreadable. The wall begins to move across the window like a fence beside a car pulling away: slowly at first, the slivers changing, then faster, until the boards blur into a translucent grey and the whole mountain is simply visible through them, steady, as the eye does with a fence at speed. The wall runs off the edge and the photograph stays, exactly as it is.
build: A transparent stage holding a repeating-linear-gradient of paper boards (60px board, 6px slit) three windows wide, translated across on one accelerating curve over about 4 s; past a speed threshold the wall's opacity falls toward 0.35 and a blur filter grows (what persistence would show), so no frame flickers; at the end the wall is off-screen, the stage empty, and o.done hands over the untouched cover.
source: Bill Brand's public-art page, the Science Friday segment 'Making Masstransiscope' (his words), Wikipedia. Descriptions only, no video.
quality: The photograph assembled by persistence: it stands whole and lit behind a wall of narrow paper slits that passes across the window at the pace of a train pulling out; at walking pace the eye gets slivers, as the slits quicken they fuse into one steady picture seen through bars, and when the wall is past the picture stays. Nearest neighbours: Rear Window's three counted blinds and the shutter curtain's one crossing slit; here many slits at speed and the eye does the work. Occluders are paper not black, the strobing phase under a second; photosensitivity is the first thing to test.

name: komorebi
pitch_zh: 畫面一開始大半在陰影裡：Aoraki 的照片在，但像被樹葉遮著，只有一枚一枚小小的光斑在上面顫動，這裡一片雪，那裡一角車窗框，每枚光斑漂移、分開，像枝葉在風裡動。眼睛跟著最亮的那一枚，把山一點一點拼起來。接著一陣風：陰影處處同時變薄，破成一個個洞，洞連成片，大約兩秒，整張照片曬在陽光下，上面什麼都不剩。
pitch_en: The window opens mostly in shadow: the Aoraki photograph is there, but under the shade of leaves, only small coins of light trembling on it, a patch of snow here, a corner of the window frame there, each coin drifting and splitting as if a branch were moving in wind. The eye follows the brightest coin and pieces the mountain together. Then a gust: the shadow thins everywhere at once, breaks into holes, the holes join, and in about two seconds the whole picture is in full sun with nothing left on it.
build: A transparent stage over the cover holding three or four full-window SVG layers of leaf-cluster shapes in the ink token at about 0.85 opacity, each drifting and wobbling on its own slow Web Animation (3 to 6 s, different phases); the gust is one timeline that scales every shape down about its own centre while the layer fades, so the shade thins and breaks rather than wipes; about 6 s in all, the stage ends empty and o.done fades it over the cover.
source: WBUR review, the Sinegang piece on the film's closing card, colorculture.org's cinematography analysis of Rashomon. Descriptions only.
quality: The photograph seen first in coins of light through leaf-shadow: the window is the photograph under a moving shadow of foliage (several layers of leaf masks drifting and trembling at different rates), the lit patches small and travelling so the eye reads the mountain in pieces; then a gust, and the shadow thins and breaks up over it until the whole picture is in sun. Not Koyaanisqatsi's one soft cloud edge, not Lux Noctis's lamp path (the sun is fixed, the stencil moves), not pane (nothing on the glass). The final clearing must thin and break, never slide off as one edge.

name: shadows
pitch_zh: 紙上有十來片撕開的紙片，站在同一條線上，亂亂的一堆，看不出什麼。一道光從左邊慢慢走過，它們的影子跟著光轉，又長又斜，彼此滑過。走到某一點，影子合起來，一瞬間就是 Aoraki 的山脊和車窗那一圈黑邊，一個你來不及解釋就認得的剪影。就在那一瞬間，影子變成照片本身的暗部，周圍被照亮的紙暖成它的天空和雪，紙片消失，整張照片就在那裡。
pitch_en: On the paper lie a dozen torn paper scraps standing on one line, a jumble, nothing in them. A light begins to walk across from the left and their shadows swing with it, long and leaning, sliding over each other. At one point the shadows meet and are, for an instant, the ridge of Aoraki and the dark edge of the car window, a silhouette you recognise before you can say why. In that instant the shadow is the photograph's own dark, the lit paper around it warms into its sky and snow, the scraps are gone, and the full picture is there.
build: The ridge silhouette (traced from the lead photograph, as tools/icons.py already does for the icon) is cut into about twelve vertical pieces; each scrap is its piece un-skewed, an SVG path standing on a baseline; per frame the light angle sweeps about 70 degrees over 3 s and each shadow is the scrap under skewX and scaleY from the baseline, so the shadows lean apart and swing into one shape at the true angle; at that frame the stage crossfades (400 ms) into the cover and o.done hands over.
source: Art of the Title page (read in full; quotes from it).
quality: Disorder that resolves under a passing light: a scatter of standing paper scraps whose shadows, as one light walks across, swing into the one silhouette of the ridge and summit, and at that instant the shadow is the photograph's own dark mass while the lit paper around it warms into its sky. Not shoji (the photograph's own silhouette, there from the first frame; here the things are not the picture and the composition exists for one angle), not the anamorphosis (there the viewer moves, here the light). Honest weakness: the last step from silhouette to photograph must come by light, not as a fill.

name: cloud
pitch_zh: 你的奧拉基照片第一刻就整張在那裡，清楚完整，只有一團柔軟的白雲蓋在山頂上。西北風把它以步行的速度往右推，尾巴漸漸變薄，山頂一道稜線一道稜線露出來。最後一絲雲從右邊滑出畫面，山站得清清楚楚：那就是首頁。
pitch_en: Your Aoraki photograph is there from the first instant, sharp and whole, except that a soft white cloud sits over the summit. The nor'west wind pushes it to the right at walking pace, its tail thinning, and the summit comes out ridge by ridge. The last of it slips off the right edge and the mountain stands clear: that is the page.
build: A transparent stage over the cover holding one SVG filter cloud (feTurbulence through a soft radial mask), translated right over about three seconds with the Web Animations API while its opacity thins in the last third; done() fires the moment its trailing edge leaves the window, the cover beneath never having changed.
source: Two landscape photographers' field notes from the mountain in his photograph (The Wandering Lens; Mark Gray: "Mt. Cook is usually hidden behind clouds, many visitors leaving without the chance to even see the peak") and the Wikipedia entry on the name; read, not watched.
quality: The summit uncovered by one passing cloud that leaves the frame, the rest of the picture never hidden: weather as the thing that passes between the viewer and the mountain.

name: alpenglow
pitch_zh: 照片以黎明前的藍色開場：冷、平，雪是灰的，湖是暗的。一抹玫瑰色落在奧拉基的最高點，順著山面往下走，先是雪原，後是岩石，從玫瑰色暖成金色，而山谷還在陰影裡。接著太陽越過你身後的山脊，湖、灌木和車窗框一口氣亮起來：整個白天，你的照片。
pitch_en: The photograph opens in pre-dawn blue: cold, flat, the snow grey, the lake dark. A touch of rose lands on the very top of Aoraki and walks down the face, snowfields first, rock after, warming from rose to gold while the valley stays in shade. Then the sun clears the ridge behind you and the lake, the scrub and the window frame take the light in one quick sweep: full daylight, your photograph.
build: Two copies of the cover on one stage: the lower graded cold with a CSS filter, the upper revealed through a canvas mask whose threshold descends a height map built from the photograph's own brightness (snow highest) with a rose-to-gold tint at the front, about two seconds, then a 400 ms whole-frame sweep; the upper copy is the untouched cover, so done() is seamless.
source: Gary Hart's field posts from the Sierra crest ("the best light on the Sierra crest usually starts a couple of minutes before the 'official' (flat horizon) sunrise"), a Light Stalking tutorial (it lasts "usually between 5 to 10 minutes") and the Wikipedia entry; read. The descent of the lit zone is from standing at a mountain at dawn.
quality: Light reaching the summit first and walking down the face, the valley lighting last and all at once: the day arriving on the mountain before it arrives on the viewer.

name: pendulum
pitch_zh: 你的照片從第一格起就靜止完整。一個黑色鏡頭蓋繫著細繩，從下緣盪上來，橫過畫面下半部盪出另一邊，再盪回來低一點，再橫過一次，每一下更短更慢，像擺錘慢慢停下。最後幾下已經搆不到畫面，鏡頭蓋露出一道邊緣就掉下去，照片就這樣被留下來。
pitch_en: Your photograph is still and whole from the first frame. From the bottom edge a dark lens cap on its thin cord swings up and across the lower picture and out the far side, comes back a little lower, crosses again, each pass shorter and slower, the way a pendulum dies. The last arcs no longer reach the frame, a final edge of the cap shows and drops away, and the photograph is simply left alone.
build: A transparent stage over the cover; an SVG disc and cord pivoted below the window follow angle = A·e^(−kt)·sin(ωt) for about 3.5 seconds, five crossings, with a short trailing copy at speed; done() when the amplitude no longer reaches the window, nothing under the stage having changed.
source: A cap-keeper maker's page ("choose how far you want the cap to hang away from the lens so it won't dangle too far or get in your way") for the photographer's event, and the Wikipedia entry on the Botafumeiro for the quality at full scale ("swings in a 65-meter arc" across the transept, maximum after "about 17 cycles"); read. The event is from use: a tethered cap swinging into the bottom of a wide frame.
quality: A passing object whose passes shorten until it leaves, the rhythm of a pendulum dying as the countdown; the picture arrives by being left alone.

name: squeegee
pitch_zh: 整個視窗是一面空白的網版：紙上蓋著細網，還沒有照片。一支橫桿從左掃到右，把整個視窗填成一片平的石灰色。停一下，刮刀從右掃回左，速度穩而均勻，刀過之處平色退去，你的奧拉基就在那裡，濕潤有光，印在紙上；光澤乾成霧面，那就是首頁。
pitch_en: The window is a blank screen: paper under a fine mesh, no photograph yet. A bar crosses left to right and floods the whole window with one flat stone colour. After a short pause the blade comes back right to left at a firm even speed, and behind it the flat colour is gone and your Aoraki is there, wet and glossy, pressed onto the paper; the gloss dries to matte and that is the page.
build: A stage with a mesh layer (repeating-linear-gradient hairlines) and a stone-coloured layer whose clip-path inset grows left to right over 900 ms behind a thin bar; after 400 ms the cover copy's clip-path inset grows right to left over 900 ms behind the blade, a white specular overlay fading over 400 ms; done() after the gloss fades, the copy being the cover itself.
source: Tate's glossary ("ink or paint is then forced through the (non-blocked areas of) open fabric with a rubber blade, known as a squeegee, onto the paper") and a press patent's background (US4817524: "the squeegee is then drawn across the mesh in a print stroke"; in the flood stroke "the squeegee is moved a certain distance above the screen, and then moved back to its starting position"; the blade "locally deforms the mesh" down onto the substrate, which lifts again behind it); read.
quality: Two strokes, out and back: the first floods the window with one flat colour, the second leaves the photograph behind the blade.

name: flood
pitch_zh: 一張空白的紙。水從一兩個點放進來，水到哪裡你的照片就出現在哪裡：它像一整片薄水衝過天空，灌進湖裡，爬上雪原，然後在稜線、灌木和車窗框的粗糙地面裡慢下來，那些邊緣最後才填滿。最後幾個深色像素填上，整張照片在同一瞬間完整，沒有任何東西需要淡出。
pitch_en: Blank paper. Water is let in at one or two points and your photograph appears wherever the flood reaches: it races across the sky as one sheet, pours into the lake, climbs the snowfields, then slows in the rough ground of the ridges, the scrub and the window frame, which fill last, edge by edge. The last dark pixels fill and the picture is whole in a single instant, with nothing left to fade.
build: At load a priority-queue flood over the 640 copy's grey levels (brightness difference as cost) assigns every pixel an arrival time; a canvas mask over the cover copy clears pixels whose time has passed with a 2 px soft front, over about 2.5 seconds; done() the instant the last pixel clears, the copy being the cover.
source: The Wikipedia entry on the watershed transform (S. Beucher and C. Lantuéjoul, 1979; Vincent and Soille's flooding algorithm, 1991): "treats the image it operates upon like a topographic map, with the brightness of each point representing its height"; the method is "placing a water source in each regional minimum in the relief, to flood the entire relief from sources, and build barriers when different water sources meet"; read.
quality: The photograph arriving in the order its own relief sets, flat regions as whole sheets, the broken edges last: the picture read by a flood.

name: chain
pitch_zh: 整個視窗是一張紙。一顆小彈珠順著摺痕滾下，碰倒一張紙卡，紙卡碰倒下一張，再放下一個繫著線的小紙鎮；每一環都看得見是前一環推動的，最後一環之前停頓一拍。線一拉，那張紙一口氣從視窗抽走，底下就是你的奧拉基，完整而安靜。
pitch_en: The window is a sheet of paper. A small marble rolls down a fold, tips a paper card, which tips another, which drops a little paper weight on a thread; each link is seen to set off the next, with one real pause before the last. The thread pulls and the paper sheet lifts off the window in one quick draw, and your Aoraki is there beneath, whole and still.
build: A paper-coloured stage carrying four small SVG pieces (a marble on an offset-path, two cards rotating about a corner, a weight falling on a thread) chained on one Web Animations timeline over about four seconds with a 600 ms pause before the last; the stage itself is the sheet and slides up out of the window in 350 ms, after which done() fires on the untouched cover.
source: Art of the Title (credits page and Top 10 of 2022 note), Peter Anderson Studio project text, Creativepool write-up, Wikipedia for Der Lauf der Dinge. Descriptions only, no video.
quality: The cause made visible: the photograph is brought by a short chain of small paper things on the page (a marble down a fold, a card tipping a card, a weight on a thread), every link seen to trigger the next, with the last link doing one plain thing the page already allows (flicking the switch of the already-approved light table, or pulling the single thread of the hikinuki find). Borrow the chain and its timing (three or four links, three to five seconds, one real pause before the last), never the burning portrait. Not a cut, not a slide into alignment, no second photograph; honest weakness is weight, so the chain must stay small and paper-coloured so the photograph wins.

name: frost
pitch_zh: 一張空白的紙，冷的。從三四個起點，稜線上、下方一角、車窗框邊，細細的枝條以結晶的角度伸出去，再分出側枝，冰長到哪裡你的照片就在冰裡。羽毛一樣的霜花變粗、相遇，到最後因為前緣很長而加快，直到整片玻璃被蓋滿，你的奧拉基就在那裡。
pitch_en: Blank paper, cold. From three or four seeds, on the ridge, in a lower corner, at the window frame, fine branches run out at the crystal's angles and throw side branches, and wherever the ice lies your photograph is in it. The ferns thicken and meet, quick at the end because the fronts are long, until the whole pane is covered and your Aoraki is simply there.
build: An offscreen canvas at quarter resolution grows branching fronts (branches at multiples of 60 degrees, side branches spawned along them, thickness growing with age) from four seeds for about four seconds; each frame it is upscaled as the alpha mask of the cover copy over paper, with a final 300 ms thickening pass so coverage reaches 100 percent by meeting; done() on full coverage.
source: Atmospheric Optics pages on fern frost (read) and Libbrecht's frost page at Caltech. Physics, no video.
quality: The photograph growing across the paper as frost grows across a pane: from three or four seeds (the ridge, a lower corner, the frame) branches run out at the crystal angles and throw side branches, each branch carrying the photograph where it lies (the ice is the picture), thickening and meeting until the sheet is covered and the cover is simply there. Canvas mask grown by branching fronts, the photograph composited through it. Not an edge crossing (many branching fronts from several seeds, meeting), not a fade, not a slide. Nearest neighbours: pane (a surface removed by a wipe; here nothing is removed, the picture itself grows) and the ink blot (a soft blob; here lines, branching, lawful). Weakness: the last gaps must close by branches meeting, never by a fill.

name: rain
pitch_zh: 一張素紙。第一滴落下，留下一個小小的濕圓，圓裡透出你的照片，像印刷品從沾濕的薄紙下透出來。雨點越來越多、越來越快，每一滴都是看向奧拉基的小圓窗，彼此重疊、相連，直到最後一陣大雨把整張紙打濕，整張照片完整安靜地在那裡。
pitch_en: Plain paper. A first drop lands and leaves a small wet disc, and inside it your photograph shows through, as a print shows through wetted tissue. Drops keep coming, faster, each a small round window onto Aoraki, overlapping and merging, until a last heavy burst wets the sheet through and the whole photograph is there and still.
build: A canvas alpha mask over the cover copy on paper: discs with a 1 px soft edge land on a schedule whose rate rises over about three seconds, each disc growing from a point in 150 ms, with a late burst sized to close every remaining gap; done() when the mask is full, the copy being the cover.
source: Art of the Title entry and its Top 10 of 2020 note (read). Description only, no video.
quality: The photograph brought up out of dry paper by drops: the page is plain, then drops land (rain, or sea spray), each making a small wet disc in which the photograph shows through the paper as a print shows through wetted tissue, the discs multiplying and merging until the sheet is wet through and the picture is whole and still. No edge crosses (the cause is drops from above, each a complete small disc, coverage from count not spread), no slide, no second photograph, and the wet sheet is the cover. Nearest neighbours: Roma (one crossing wash, cut for the edge; here no wash), pane (drops on glass over the view, wiped; here the drops are the reveal, no glass, no wipe), the ink blot (one blob). Weakness: the last dry gaps must be closed by a late heavier burst of drops, never a fade.
